unsupported_claims: If the method uses transition probabilities proportional to w^γ, increasing γ sharpens bias toward heavier edges (speculative; in the paper γ is the number of random walks per vertex, not an exponent)
The effect diminishes when edge weights are near uniform because γ then has no effect (not in evidence and based on wrong definition of γ)
The effect levels off at extreme values where the walk becomes nearly deterministic (not in evidence; contradicts the actual finding that it slows after γ > 10)
rationale: The LINE claim (sampling edges proportional to weight) is supported, but the answer misdefines γ as a weight exponent, whereas the paper defines it as the number of walks per vertex, with diminishing returns beyond γ > 10. The core explanation of γ's effect and when it diminishes is therefore unsupported and misses the key finding that the effect slows once γ exceeds 10; the answer also omits the conversion to binary edges.
